name: ClaudeCodeMonitor
headline: Claude Code监控器
short_description: A  lightweight macOS menu bar application that monitors and manages Claude Code instances in real-time. Keep track of multiple Claude sessions, their resource usage, and running processes - all from your menu bar.
author: Aura-Technologies-llc

sections.overview:
ClaudeCodeMonitor is a native macOS menu bar application designed for developers working with Claude Code. It automatically detects and tracks multiple Claude Code instances, displaying live CPU and memory consumption alongside active commands and task status. The app enables quick instance management—rename, focus, or kill processes—directly from your menu bar while receiving notifications when long-running tasks complete. Built with native macOS APIs and Apple-notarized for security, it requires minimal system resources and operates entirely locally with no data collection.
Track multiple Claude coding sessions during active development
Monitor CPU and memory usage across Claude instances to prevent system slowdowns
Get notifications when long-running builds, tests, or deployments complete
Switch between different Claude instances working on separate projects
- **Developers**: Monitor and manage multiple Claude Code instances simultaneously.
- **System Administrators**: Ensure optimal resource usage and system performance.
- **Data Scientists**: Track and manage complex data processing tasks.
sections.setup:
No install command available. Check the GitHub repository for manual installation instructions.
`git clone https://github.com/Aura-Technologies-llc/ClaudeCodeMonitor`
sections.usage:
```
Create a lightweight macOS menu bar application called ClaudeCodeMonitor that monitors and manages Claude Code instances in real-time for [COMPANY]. The app should track multiple Claude sessions, their resource usage, and running processes. Include features like session naming, resource usage graphs, and process termination. Ensure the design is clean and intuitive, with a focus on real-time updates and minimal system overhead.
```
